gaps.text: In-line measurement of temperature at the probe with temperature sensor (bioreactor)

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion of the UV-Vis and fluorescence blocks is the starting hypothesis, with block scaling so that neither block dominates; the two methods sample different depths, so the information must come from the same small spot. Acquisition rates differ, so both blocks must be normalised to a common time step and each block keeps its own calibration and diagnostics. The fused model must beat the best single-method model on held-out runs, otherwise the extra channel is dropped.)

Whether an in-line UV-Vis probe can report viable cell concentration in a mammalian culture medium: the material covers biomass-related turbidity and UV-ATR for high-optical-density fluids, but not viability in mammalian media.
Probe sterilisation, autoclaving and clean-in-place/steam-in-place compatibility inside a stirred bioreactor, and fouling behaviour over a batch.

items.finding: The review states that optical fiber sensors for bioreactor parameters briefly cover temperature monitoring.
items.how_it_applies: This supports considering an optical fiber temperature sensor at the probe location alongside the UV-Vis measurement, so temperature can be logged with the spectra.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is an abstract-only review with emphasis on pH and dissolved oxygen; it does not show integration with a UV-Vis probe or performance in a stirred mammalian bioreactor.

citation.quote: This review summarizes recent progress in optical fiber sensors for key bioreactor parameters, with an emphasis on pH and dissolved oxygen (DO), and briefly covers temperature and pressure monitoring.
citation.label: E05 ¶1

items.finding: The source describes a multi-sensor chip that includes measurement of temperature (T sensor), pH (ISFET), and dissolved oxygen concentration.
items.how_it_applies: This indicates that temperature sensing can be combined with other in-line sensors in a bioreactor sensor array, which is relevant to adding temperature at the probe.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The work is on a micro bioreactor sensor chip, not a stirred mammalian bioreactor or a UV-Vis fiber probe, so integration and scale differ.

citation.quote: measurement of temperature (T sensor), pH (ISFET), dissolved oxygen concentration
citation.label: E04 ¶2727

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This matches the starting hypothesis of low-level fusion of UV-Vis and fluorescence blocks; it informs how the fused matrix could be built before testing whether it improves over the best single method.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a general PAT data-fusion review, not a UV-Vis/fluorescence bioreactor study, and it does not address block scaling or differing acquisition rates.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: The source says that before fusing data from multiple sources, the contribution of each dataset and its complementarity should be evaluated.
items.how_it_applies: This supports testing each block's contribution and requiring the fused model to beat the best single-method model on held-out runs before keeping the extra channel.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The recommendation is general and does not specify UV-Vis and fluorescence blocks, block scaling, or a common time step for different acquisition rates.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: The source refers to spectroscopy as a technique for on-line monitoring of viable cell concentrations.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that spectroscopy-based on-line viable cell monitoring is a recognized topic, so an in-line UV-Vis probe could be evaluated for viable cell concentration in the customer's medium.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source is a micro bioreactor sensor-array thesis and does not specify UV-Vis, mammalian cells, or the customer's medium; it is not evidence that the probe will work here.

citation.quote: spectroscopy as a technique for on-line monitoring of viable cell concentrations.
citation.label: E04 ¶203

items.finding: The source notes that accurate measurement may not be possible because the probe window can be contaminated by a binder added during the process.
items.how_it_applies: This highlights probe-window fouling as a risk to watch over a batch, so fouling behaviour should be tested for the UV-Vis probe in the medium.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The example is a pharmaceutical process with a binder, not a mammalian cell culture or a UV-Vis fiber probe, and it does not cover sterilisation, autoclaving, CIP, or SIP.

citation.quote: However, an accurate measurement may not be possible because of contamination of the probe window due to the addition of a binder during the process, which is a disadvantage.
citation.label: E03 ¶27
